STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.claim: God's enduring reality offsets the dualities: verses 26–27 stress that God remains while everything else passes away.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.anchor: vv. 26–27, which emphasize that God remains while all else fades away

STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.claim: Verse 27 is echoed by verse 78, showing that God transcends both earthly and heavenly blessings.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r12.anchor: V. 27 is then echoed in the last verse (v. 78)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.claim: Only God is immortal; all other beings perish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.anchor: God alone is immortal and all the rest are mortal.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r3.claim: The pronoun in ‘upon it’ refers back to the earth discussed since verse 10.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r3.anchor: The antecedent of the genitive pronoun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.claim: The created order, provision, divine wisdom, sovereignty, and harmony entail that all creation will end and only God remain; all will be judged without being able to challenge His decisions or intercede without permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.anchor: Only the exalted and revered person of God will remain. Everyone will be gathered before Him one day and He will deal with everyone in the manner that person is worthy of.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.claim: The repeated phrase ‘Lord of majesty and bounty’ at the end of the sūrah indicates that only God is exalted, revered, and without a partner in these attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r5.anchor: The purpose of mentioning both these words is that only He is exalted in His being and thus only He is worthy of being respected and revered by all.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r6.claim: Wajh (‘face’) means God’s person because the face, as the highest part, can stand for the whole person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r6.anchor: face) here signifies the person of God. Face is the most lofty portion of a being; for this reason, at times, it signifies the whole person.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.claim: Perishing means the extinction of every created thing, while face denotes a thing's reality; God is exempt from bodily limbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.anchor: والفناء عبارة عن إعدام جميع الموجودات من حيوان وغيره، والوجه يعبر به عن حقيقة الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r4.claim: The Quraysh poor used face idiomatically to ask where a generous Arab was who would give them aid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r4.anchor: وتقول صعاليك مكة: أين وجه عربي كريم يجود علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r5.claim: Most readers use dhū with wāw as an adjective for wajh; Abū and ʿAbd Allāh read dhī with yāʾ as an adjective for the Lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ذو بالواو، وصفة للوجه وأبي وعبد الله: ذي بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r6.claim: The apparent addressee in your Lord's face is the Prophet, which specially honors him; another view makes the address general to every listener.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في قوله: وجه ربك للرسول، وفيه تشريف عظيم له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r7.claim: Dhu al-jalāl is explained as the one whom monotheists exalt above likeness to creation and their deeds, the one whose majesty inspires awe, or the giver of majesty and honor to sincere servants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r7.anchor: ومعنى ذو الجلال: الذي يجله الموحدون عن التشبيه بخلقه وعن أفعالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.claim: The ending of worldly blessings with the enduring face matches the end of afterlife blessings with the blessed name: permanence suits the world's passing, while growth suits the increase and duration of Paradise's gifts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p72/r5.anchor: ختم تعالى نعم الدنيا بقوله: ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام، ختم نعم الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.claim: Calling the surviving entity ‘the Lord’ might imply He remains as Lord with a subject; saying ‘His face’ removes that implication and asserts the Real’s absolute permanence.
RAZI-FULL:v29p120#2/r6.anchor: لو قال : ويبقى الرب لتوهم أن الرب إذا بقي ربا فله في ذلك الزمان مربوب

NAHHAS:v4p308/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p308/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p308/r3.claim: ذو modifies وجه; the intended sense is that your Lord remains, like the expression “the face of the earth.”
NAHHAS:v4p308/r3.anchor: ذو من نعت وجه لأن المعنى ويبقى ربك كما تقول هذا وجه الأرض

NAHHAS:v4p308/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p308/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v4p308/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reads ذي الجلال والإكرام, making it an adjective of ربك.
NAHHAS:v4p308/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود ( ويبقى وجه ربك ذي الجلال والإكرام ) من نعت ربك

SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r1.claim: The common reading has ذو nominative as an adjective of وجه; Ubayy and Abd Allah read ذي genitive as an adjective of ربك.
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r1.anchor: العامة على " ذو " بالواو صفة للوجه. وأبي وعبد الله " ذي " بالياء صفة ل " ربك

SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r2.claim: Al-Samin notes that the seven readers differ again on this phrase at the end of the sura.
SAMIN-DURR:55:27/r2.anchor: وسيأتي خلاف بين السبعة في آخر السورة إن شاء الله تعالى

ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r3.claim: God's Self alone abides forever, in majesty and glory.
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r3.anchor: but forever will abide thy Sustainer's Self, [11] full of majesty and glory

ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r1.claim: Classical Arabic uses face or countenance metonymically for a person's self or whole being; here it denotes God's essential Being or Reality.
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r1.anchor: a term used metonymically in classical Arabic to denote

ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r2.claim: Asad compares 28:88, which says everything perishes except God's eternal Self.
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n11/r2.anchor: Everything isbound to perish, save His [eternal] Self

NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.speaker: الشعبي
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says not to pause after kullu man ʿalayhā fān until reciting wa-yabqā wajhu rabbika dhu al-jalāli wa-l-ikrām.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.anchor: وصح عندنا عن الشعبي، وهو من أئمة التابعين علما وفقها ومقتدى أنه قال: إذا قرأت كل من عليها فان

NASHR:v2p382/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p382/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p382/r2.claim: All readers use wāw in the first occurrence, wa-yabqā wajhu rabbika dhu al-jalāl; it modifies wajh and cannot be an insertion, as all codices agree.
NASHR:v2p382/r2.anchor: (واتفقوا) على الواو في الحرف الأول، وهو قوله ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال نعتا للوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r1.claim: Al-Alusi interprets God’s face as His essence, with a descriptive attribution; using a bodily face for essence is a common metonym, like ‘hands’ for persons.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r1.anchor: أي ذاته عز وجل والمراد هو سبحانه وتعالى فالإضافة بيانية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r2.claim: Another view says face originally means direction and its use for essence is allusive; al-Alusi identifies the essence interpretation with later theologians’ taʾwil, unlike the Salaf’s method.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : أصله الجهة واستعماله في الذاتمن باب الكناية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r3.claim: The address apparently honors the Prophet; another view addresses anyone suited to receive the grave message.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في ربك للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r4.claim: Some take face as intention, meaning deeds intended for God; al-Alusi finds this problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r4.anchor: ما قيل : الوجه بمعنى القصد ويراد به المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r5.claim: A closer alternative takes face as the direction God commanded people to face and approach: righteous deeds remain for reward, but this does not fit the context of universal perishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r5.anchor: وأقرب منه ما قيل : وجهه تعالى الجهة التي أمرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r6.claim: Another view makes the face the divine direction God attends to and bestows; that aspect remains while each thing itself perishes continually.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : وجهه سبحانه الجهة التي يليها الحق أي يتولاها بفضله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r7.claim: A metaphysical reading takes God’s face as a possible being’s relation to Him; considered independent of the true existent that causes it, the possible is nonexistent.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : المراد بوجهه سبحانه وجهه الممكن وهي جهة حيثية ارتباطه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r8.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r8.claim: Al-Bayḍawi says all aspects of beings perish in themselves except the aspect turned toward God; scholars differ whether this continues his earlier essence interpretation or adds another.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r8.anchor: وقول العلامة البيضاوي : لو استقرت جهات الموجودات وتفحصت وجوهها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r9.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes actual existence inhering in possibles (most philosophers and theologians) from metaphorical existence; the latter divides into the ‘theistic’ philosophers’ manifestation model and realized Sufis’ one-essence model.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r9.anchor: وذلك أنها إما موجودة حقيقة بمعنى أنها متصفة بالوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r10.speaker: المتألهون من الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r10.claim: For the ‘theistic’ philosophers, possibles are mirrors manifesting self-subsistent divine existence; their differing relation to the Necessary gives distinct reflections, and paths to God equal creatures’ breaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r10.anchor: وإليه ذهب المتأهلون من الحكماء والمحققون من الصوفية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r11.speaker: المحققون من الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r11.claim: Realized Sufis posit one essence with multiple attributes, aspects, and renewed manifestations, rather than multiple necessary and possible essences; the two mystical accounts are commonly treated alike.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r11.anchor: ومذاق المحققين من الصوفية أن علاقة المجاز أنها بمنزلة صفات قائمة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r12.claim: On the real-existence view, face is existence bestowed on possibles by the Necessary through ‘necessity by another,’ the honored aspect nearest intrinsic necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#3/r12.anchor: ووجه التطبيق على الول أن يقال : المراد من الوجه الذي يلي جهته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r1.claim: On the philosophers’ metaphorical account, face is the special relation to the divine presence that permits calling a possible existent, as God’s manifestation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r1.anchor: ووجه التطبيقعلى الثاني أن يقال : الوجه الذي يلي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r2.claim: On the realized Sufi account, created things are nonexistent in every respect except as divine affairs and considerations.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r2.anchor: ووجه التطبيق على الثالث أن يقالأ : المراد بالوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r3.claim: The phrase can describe the awe monotheists feel before God, His intrinsic perfection beyond comprehension, or His majesty and generosity toward them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r3.anchor: أي يجله الموحدون عن التشبيه بخلقه ويثبتون له ما يليق بشأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r4.claim: Some scholars gloss majesty as absolute independence and generosity as complete favor; majesty entails transcendence and needlessness, as al-Jawhari notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r4.anchor: وفسر بعض المحققين ( الجلال ) بالأستغناء المطلق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r5.speaker: الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r5.claim: Al-Kirmani classifies negative attributes such as having no partner as majesty and positive attributes such as life and knowledge as generosity; al-Alusi says this needs examination.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r5.anchor: وقال الكرماني : إنه تعالى لهصفات عدمية مثل ( لا شريك له )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r6.claim: ذو apparently modifies face: creation’s extinction cannot impair God’s self-sufficiency, and He will bestow generosity on humans and jinn after they perish.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن ( ذو ) صفة للوجه ويتضمن الوصف بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r7.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r7.claim: If face means righteous action or direction, some parse ذو as a detached predicate referring to the Lord; the genitive reading ذي by Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud supports attachment to Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r7.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة أبي وعبد الله ذيالجلال بالياء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r8.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says this title belongs uniquely to God and is among His greatest descriptions.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r8.anchor: وذكر الراغب أن هذا الوصف قد خص به عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r9.speaker: أنس وربيعة بن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r9.claim: Raised reports from Anas and Rabiʿa ibn ʿAmir urge frequent invocation of this name; al-Alusi explains ألظوا as adhering to and repeating it in supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r9.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي عن أنس والإمام أحمد عن ربيعة بن عامر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r10.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r10.claim: Anas reports a man’s supplication using this name; the Prophet says he invoked God by His greatest name, by which He answers and grants requests.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p109/r10.anchor: وروي الترمذي وأبو داود والنسائي عن أنس أنه كان مع رسول الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r3.claim: The enduring “face” is God's essence: created things are finite in themselves, except God's face, the aspect facing His direction.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r4.claim: ذو الجلال والإكرام means absolute self-sufficiency and general bounty.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r1.claim: The face is the noblest part of a being and can stand for its possessor; since it cannot remain apart from its possessor, it conveys the continued existence of the whole after creation perishes.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r1.anchor: الوجه أشرف ما في الوجود , وكان بعر به عما أريد به صاحب الوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r2.claim: God remains forever after all else perishes. ‘Your Lord’s face’ refers to his essence, the noblest aspect of his being; the wording is more eloquent than ‘its possessor.’
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r2.anchor: أي بعد فناء الكل , بقاء مستمرا إلى ما لا نهاية له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r3.claim: The Lord is the one who nurtures the Prophet through the message and revelation toward boundless knowledge; seeking his face also means acting sincerely for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r3.anchor: أي المربي لك بالرسالة والترقية بهذا الوحي إلى ما لا يحد من المعارف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r4.claim: The religious principle that nothing resembles God prevents a corporeal reading of ‘face’; God is free of need and deficiency, unlike all observable creatures.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r4.anchor: وكان من المقرر عند أهل الشرع أنه سبحانه ليس كمثله شيء فلا يتوهم أحد منهم من التعبير به نقصا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r5.claim: ‘Possessor of majesty’ describes God’s essence: unsurpassable greatness that excludes everything unworthy of him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r5.anchor: أي العظمة التي لا ترام وهو صفة ذاته التي تقتضي إجلاله عن كل ما لا يليق به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r6.claim: ‘And honor’ describes God’s action, his general beneficence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p385/r6.anchor: أي الإحسان العام وهو صفة فعله

DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī advises readers not to stop after the statement that all on earth perish, but to continue through the statement that God's face remains.
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ {ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام}

DURR-FULL:v7p698/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ذو الجلال والإكرام as possessing majesty and greatness.
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ذو الجلال والإكرام} قال: ذو الكبرياء والعظمة

DURR-FULL:v7p698/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r5.speaker: رجل
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r5.claim: A man prayed for God's sufficient, generous face; al-Bayhaqī's wording instead calls it the abiding, beautiful face.
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r5.anchor: عن حميد بن هلال قال: قال رجل: يرحم الله رجلا أتى على هذه الآية {ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.claim: Everyone on earth will perish; the reminder of death points beyond it to the reckoning and recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أن مصير جميع من على الأرض إلى الفناء ، وهذا تذكير بالموت وما بعده من الجزاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r5.claim: وجه ربك means God's essence; in Arabic usage face can stand for the whole person or self, as al-Kashshaf notes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r5.anchor: و { وجه ربك } : ذاته ، فذكر الوجه هنا جار على عرف كلام العرب . قال في ( الكشاف ) : والوجه يعبر به عن الجملة والذات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r6.claim: The Quran uses وجه الله in other senses as well, in the direction toward which people turn and in the intention of acts of charity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r6.anchor: وقد أضيف إلى اسمه تعالى لفظ الوجه بمعان مختلفة منها ما هنا ومنها قوله : { فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله } ( البقرة : 115 ) وقوله : { إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r7.claim: Listeners know that God cannot literally possess a face as a bodily part of the head.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r7.anchor: وقد علم السامعون أن الله تعالى يستحيل أن يكون له وجه بالمعنى الحقيقي وهو الجزء الذي في الرأس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r8.speaker: السلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r8.claim: The early Muslims treated such expressions as ambiguous and refrained from interpreting them, while remaining certain that their apparent bodily sense is impossible for God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r8.anchor: وكان السلف يحجمون عن الخوض في ذلك مع اليقين باستحالة ظاهره على الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r9.speaker: علماء التابعين ومن بعدهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r9.claim: Successor and later scholars gradually interpreted such expressions using the principles of rhetoric, making their meaning clear; Ibn ʿĀshūr regards both early restraint and later interpretation as sound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r9.anchor: ثم تناوله علماء التابعين ومن بعدهم بالتأويل تدريجا إلى أن اتضح وجه التأويل بالجري على قواعد علم المعاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r10.claim: The address is to the Prophet, honoring his rank, while its intended audience is everyone who hears the Quran; it may instead address any hearer generally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r10.anchor: وضمير المخاطب في قوله : { وجه ربك } خطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيه تعظيم لقدر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r11.claim: Because وجه means the divine essence, it can be described by majesty and generosity: these cover all attributes of transcendence, perfection, beauty, and beneficence toward servants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r11.anchor: ولما كان الوجه هنا بمعنى الذات وصف ب { ذو الجلال } ، أي العظمة و { الإكرام } ، أي المنعم على عباده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that your Lord remains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r1.anchor: ويبقى وجه ربك أي ويبقى ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi explains jalal and ikram as verbal nouns: God deserves reverence and honor, and must not be denied or disbelieved.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي الجلال مصدر الجليل يقال جليل بين الجلالة والجلال والإكرام مصدر أكرم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r3.claim: Another possible sense is that God honors those devoted to Him and raises their ranks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r3.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المعنى أنه يكرم أهل ولايته ويرفع درجاتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r4.claim: He also allows one term to describe God’s attribute and the other the servant’s act, as in 74:56: God is worthy of forgiveness and people are to be pious.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114#2/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى هو أهل التقوى وأهل المغفرة المدثر 56 فانصرف أحد الأمرين إلى الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.claim: Qatada says God first informed people about what He created, then informed them that all of it would pass away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: أنبأ بما خلق، ثم أنبأ أن ذلك كله كان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a transmitted supplication calling God the Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, Creator of the heavens and earth, and the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, asking for mercy, rectitude, and protection from reliance on self or creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r3.anchor: يا حي، يا قيوم، يا بديع السموات والأرض، يا ذا الجلال والإكرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says one should not stop after reciting that all on earth perish, but continue through the declaration that God's Face remains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} ، فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r5.claim: The verse parallels 28:88, that everything perishes except God's Face, and connects seeking God's Face with worship and charity in 18:28 and 76:9.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية كقوله تعالى: {كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه} [القصص:88]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r6.claim: God's Face is characterized by Majesty and Honor: God is worthy to be revered without disobedience and obeyed without defiance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r6.anchor: هو أهل أن يجل فلا يعصى، وأن يطاع فلا يخالف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Possessor of Majesty and Honor as Possessor of greatness and pride.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {ذو الجلال والإكرام} ذو العظمة والكبرياء

JISHUMI:v9p6714/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6714/r4.speaker: عبد الله
JISHUMI:v9p6714/r4.claim: Abdullah reads ذي, making the phrase an adjective of the Lord; the common ذُو is an adjective of وجه.
JISHUMI:v9p6714/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: ذو الجلال بالواو على أنه صفة الوجه، وعن عبد الله: ذي الجلال، على أنها نعت الرب

MUQATIL:55:24-28/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r5.claim: God's face remains; all creatures in the heavens and earth die except God's face, meaning God himself.
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r5.anchor: كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه [القصص: 88]، يعني كل شىء من الحيوان في السماوات والأرض يموت إلا وجهه

MUQATIL:55:24-28/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r6.claim: When the verse descended, the angels in heaven said the people of earth had perished and wondered how life could benefit them; God's statement in 28:88 assured them all would die.
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r6.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية، قالت الملائكة الذين في السماء: هلك أهل الأرض العجب لهم كيف تنفعهم المعيشة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r1.claim: “The Face of your Lord” means His essence.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ ويبقى وجه ربك ﴾ ذاته ﴿ ذو الجلال ﴾ ذو العظمة والسلطان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r2.claim: Dhu al-jalāl means possessing majesty and sovereignty; it grammatically describes the Face.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r2.anchor: ذو العظمة والسلطان وهو صفة الوجه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r3.claim: Al-ikrām means pardon and beneficence; this is one of God's mighty attributes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r3.anchor: بالتجاوز والاحسان وهذه الصفة من عظيم صفات الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r4.claim: A hadith urges persistent invocation with the words “O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r4.anchor: وفى الحديث الظوا بباذا الجلال ولاكرام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r5.claim: The Prophet passed a man praying and saying this invocation, and told him that his prayer had been answered.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#3/r5.anchor: وروى انه عليه السلام مر بجل وهو يصلى ويقول باذا الجلال والاكرام فقال قد استجيب لك

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r5.speaker: ابن فورك وأبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r5.claim: The author endorses scholars who take God’s face to mean His existence and essence, which alone remains when creation perishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r5.anchor: وهذا الذي ارتضاه المحققون من علمائنا: ابن فورك وأبو المعالي وغيرهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas takes face as a reference to God Himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الوجه عبارة عنه كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r7.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r7.claim: Abu al-Maʿali says most imams understand face as the Creator’s existence; its endurance when creatures perish supports this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r7.anchor: وأما الوجه فالمراد به عند معظم أئمتنا وجود الباري تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r8.claim: The commentary refers readers to its discussion of 2:115 and fuller treatment in al-Kitāb al-Asnā.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r8.anchor: وقد مضى في «البقرة» القول في هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r9.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r9.claim: Al-Qushayri reports a view that face is an additional, unqualified attribute through which God turns toward those He chooses to honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r9.anchor: قال القشيري: قال قوم هو صفة زائدة على الذات لا تكيف

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r10.claim: The author says the sounder view is that face means God’s existence and essence, as in idioms meaning the point or essence of a matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r10.anchor: والصحيح أن يقال: وجهه وجوده وذاته، يقال: هذا وجه الأمر

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r11.claim: Other interpretations are that what remains is God made manifest by His proofs, or the direction through which people draw near to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r11.anchor: وقيل: أي يبقى الظاهر بأدلته كظهور الإنسان بوجهه. وقيل: وتبقى الجهة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r12.claim: Jalāl means God’s majesty, greatness, and entitlement to attributes of praise; the word derives from jalla, to be great.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r12.anchor: الجلال عظمة الله وكبرياؤه واستحقاقه صفات المدح

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r13.claim: Ikram means God deserves reverence and should be declared free of what is unbefitting, such as associating partners with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r13.anchor: أي هو أهل لأن يكرم عما لا يليق به من الشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet urging people to persistently invoke God as Possessor of Majesty and Honor.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r2.claim: The invocation is also attributed to Ibn Masud and is explained as clinging to that formula in supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r2.anchor: وروي أنه من قول ابن مسعود ومعناه: الزموا ذلك في الدعاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd explains ilẓāẓ as adhering persistently to something, also meaning insistent supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: الإلظاظ لزوم الشيء والمثابرة عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r4.speaker: سعيد المقبري
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r4.claim: Saʿid al-Maqburi tells of a man repeatedly invoking God by this name and hearing that his request had been heard.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-28/r4.anchor: وعن سعيد المقبري: أن رجلا ألح فجعل يقول

QASHANI:55:19-27/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:19-27/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:19-27/r10.claim: The face that remains after creation’s passing is God’s essence together with all His attributes.

QASHANI:55:19-27/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:19-27/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:19-27/r11.claim: Divine majesty is greatness and exaltation: God veils Himself with luminous and dark veils and manifests through dominion and overpowering.
QASHANI:55:19-27/r11.anchor: العظمة والعلو بالاحتجاب بالحجب النورانية والظلمانية والظهور بصفة القهر والسلطنة

QASHANI:55:19-27/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:19-27/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:19-27/r12.claim: Divine generosity is nearness through manifestations of the attributes, and the essence’s appearance through gentleness and mercy.
QASHANI:55:19-27/r12.anchor: بالقرب والدنو في صور تجليات الصفات وعند ظهورالذات بصفة اللطف والرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.claim: Razi rejects the corporealist reading of face as an organ: 28:88 says only God's face remains, which would imply that His other bodily parts perish; the sound reading is God's essence, which alone remains.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r1.anchor: الوجه يطلق على الذات والمجسم يحمل الوجه على العضو وهو خلاف العقل والنقل أعني القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.claim: Against the objection that identifying face with essence erases divine attributes, Razi argues that speech about a remaining garment includes its color and dimensions; likewise God's essence includes His attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r2.anchor: لم يبق لفلان إلا ثوب يتناول الثوب وما قام به من اللون والطول والعرض

RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.claim: Face is used for a person's whole reality because people say they have seen someone upon seeing the face: its many organs let perception infer more about the person than seeing a hand or foot.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r3.anchor: فإن الوجه يستعمل في العرف لحقيقة الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r4.claim: Razi rejects the claim in some legal books that face derives from confrontation: the organ-name came first, and related forms were derived from it by later transfer.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93#2/r4.anchor: إن الوجه من المواجهة كما هو المسطور في البعض من الكتب الفقهية

RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r1.claim: No other divine name works in place of face: known names such as Lord, Creator, and Provider are agent-names, while Allah is sometimes glossed as the worshipped one; calling Him your Lord remaining could suggest a continuing lorded-over object.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r1.anchor: ما كان يقوم مقام الوجه لفظ آخر

RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r2.claim: Face of Allah in 2:115 and 30:38 refers to worship: the first passage concerns prayer and the second charity to kin, poor people, and travelers; here, where God's sustaining bounties are discussed, the wording is face of your Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94/r2.anchor: المراد في الموضعين المذكورين هو العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r1.claim: The address most likely reaches every listener: each should attend to God alone, since everything besides Him perishes.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه مع كل أحد كأنه يقول : ويبقى وجه ربك

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r2.claim: He also allows that the address may be directed specifically to Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الخطاب مع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r3.claim: The singular address includes each hearer while underscoring universal perishability; a dual address could let each addressee exempt himself and his companion.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r3.anchor: ولو قال : وجه ربكما لكان كل واحد يخرج نفسه ورفيقه المخاطب من الفناء

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r4.claim: Direct address to the Lord signals gentleness while the statement of abiding signals might; the context enumerates kindness and favors.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r4.anchor: كأن الخطاب في الرب إشارة إلى اللطف والإبقاء إشارة إلى القهر

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r5.claim: Rabb is customarily used in an annexed construction; when unannexed, it is paired with another description, as in the cited verses.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r5.anchor: وفي لفظ الرب عادة جارية وهي أنه لا يترك استعماله مع الإضافة

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r6.claim: Rabb may be a verbal noun meaning upbringing, as in the verbs for raising or nurturing.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r6.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون مصدرا بمعنى التربية ، يقال : ربه يربه ربا مثل رباه يربيه

RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, rabb may be an adjective derived from a verbal noun meaning one who nurtures, by analogy with names of agents and qualities.
RAZI-FULL:v29p94#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون وصفا من الرب الذي هو مصدر بمعنى الراب كالطب للطبيب

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.claim: The passage recalls 28:88, where all things perish except God’s Face.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.anchor: Cf. 28:88: All things perish, save His Face

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.claim: These verses turn the sūrah from earthly blessings in vv. 10–25 to the blessings of the Hereafter in the remaining verses.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.anchor: These verses mark an important turn in this sūrah, as vv. 10–25 refer to the blessings or boons of this world

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r4.claim: Grammatically, “Possessed of Majesty and Bounty” describes the Face.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r4.anchor: Grammatically itis the Face that is Possessed of Majesty

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r5.claim: Because wajh can denote a thing’s essence, the Face here refers to God’s Being and Essence.

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r6.speaker: some theologians
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r6.claim: Theologians distinguishing Essence from Attributes infer that God’s Attributes also pass away, leaving only the Divine Essence.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r6.anchor: Some theologians who see a distinction between God’s Attributes and God’s Essence maintain that this verse indicates that God’s Attributes will also “pass away”

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r7.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that this interpretation would require the wording “nothing remains except the Face of thy Lord.”
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r7.anchor: Al-Rāzī, however, maintains that for this to be the meaning, one would need to say, “And there remains nothing except the Face of thy Lord.”

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r8.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r8.claim: Some explain the choice of “thy Lord” rather than “God” as closer to this sūrah’s theme of blessing and bounty.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r8.anchor: According to some, the Face of thy Lord is used instead of the Face of God, which is used in several other verses

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r9.claim: Majesty and Bounty can refer respectively to God’s Attributes of Majesty and Beauty, a common theological division of the Divine Names and Attributes.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r9.anchor: The use of Majesty and Bounty can be seen as a reference to God’s Attributes of Majesty and God’s Attributes of Beauty

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r10.speaker: many Shiites
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r10.claim: Many Shiites call Beauty the positive attributes inherent in God’s Essence and expressing perfection; Majesty negates limiting physical qualities, thereby reaffirming positive attributes.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r10.anchor: For many Shiites the Attributes of Beauty are those positive attributes that are inherent in God’s Essence

TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.claim: All jinn and humans on the earth will perish, while God's face remains, possessing majesty and honor.
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.anchor: الجلال والإكرام؛ وذو الجلال والإكرام من نعت الوجه فلذلك رفع ذو

TAB-FULL:v22p212/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r2.claim: Al-Tabari parses ذو as an adjective of وجه, explaining its nominative form.
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r2.anchor: وذو الجلال والإكرام من نعت الوجه فلذلك رفع ذو

TAB-FULL:v22p212/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r3.claim: Abdullah's reading has ذي in the genitive, making it an adjective of the Lord rather than of the face.
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر أنها في قراءة عبد الله بالياء «ذي الجلال والإكرام» على أنه من نعت الرب وصفته

SULAMI:v2p294#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p294#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p294#3/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says God hides Himself from the elect who witness Him, unlike ordinary people; in this life He gives according to what He discloses inwardly and veils through His wonders, while in the next He gives outwardly and veils through what creatures can bear, hiding Himself only by shielding them from His vision.
SULAMI:v2p294#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : الذي أخفى من شاهده للخاصة ولا يظهره للعوام فسئل أفرق بين الدارين ؟ قال : نعم اعطاهم في الدنيا

TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.claim: Perishing and the advent of the life of recompense are favors, since worldly life is a preliminary stage for the afterlife; this answers the objection that perishing cannot be a favor.
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.anchor: وكلاهما أعني فناء من عليها وطلوع نشأة الجزاء عليهم من النعم والآلاء

TABATABAI:55:27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r2.claim: A thing’s face is what it turns toward others or what others turn toward in it.
TABATABAI:55:27/r2.anchor: وجه الشيء ما يستقبل به غيره ويقصده به غيره

TABATABAI:55:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r3.claim: God’s face denotes His noble attributes, intermediaries between Him and creation through which blessings such as creating, governing, mercy, and provision reach creatures.
TABATABAI:55:27/r3.anchor: صفاته الكريمة التي تتوسط بينه وبين خلقه فتنزل بها عليهم البركات من خلق وتدبير

TABATABAI:55:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r4.claim: Jalal concerns exalted, repelling or withholding qualities; ikram concerns beautiful qualities that attract, including life, mercy, generosity, and beauty.
TABATABAI:55:27/r4.anchor: في الجلال شيء من معنى الاعتلاء والترفع المعنوي على الغير فيناسب من الصفات

TABATABAI:55:27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r5.claim: The name ذو الجلال والإكرام combines the names of majesty and beauty, and in truth names the sacred Essence.
TABATABAI:55:27/r5.anchor: اسم من الأسماء الحسنى جامع بمفهومه بين أسماء الجمال وأسماء الجلال جميعا

TABATABAI:55:27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r6.claim: The description may be detached from its grammatical role for praise, with an implied predicate: He is the Possessor of majesty and honor.
TABATABAI:55:27/r6.anchor: وهو إما لكونه وصفا مقطوعا عن الوصفية للمدح

TABATABAI:55:27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r7.claim: Alternatively, face means God’s noble attribute or sacred name, so applying the name to the name ultimately applies it to the Essence.
TABATABAI:55:27/r7.anchor: لأن المراد بالوجه كما تقدم هو صفته الكريمة واسمه المقدس وإجراء الاسم على الاسم

TABATABAI:55:27/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r8.claim: If face means the divine name, God remains with His majesty and honor, and the creatures’ perishing changes nothing in Him.
TABATABAI:55:27/r8.anchor: ويبقى ربك عز اسمه بما له من الجلال والإكرام من غير أن يؤثر فناؤهم

TABATABAI:55:27/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r9.claim: If face means what creatures direct themselves toward in God’s sphere, what remains after worldly people perish includes prophets, saints, religion, reward, and nearness to God.
TABATABAI:55:27/r9.anchor: كل ما ينتسب إليه تعالى فيكون مقصودا بنحو للمتوجه إليه كأنبيائه وأوليائه ودينه

TABRISI:55:24-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r7.claim: “The face of your Lord” means the Lord Himself, enduring and manifest through His proofs as a person's face makes him manifest.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r7.anchor: ويبقى ربك الظاهر بأدلته ظهور الإنسان بوجهه

TABRISI:55:24-29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r8.claim: Majesty denotes greatness, deserving praise, and supreme beneficence, the source of every favor; God honors prophets and friends with His subtle favors.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r8.anchor: أي العظمة والكبرياء واستحقاق الحمد والمدح بإحسانه

TABRISI:55:24-29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:55:24-29/r9.claim: Alternatively, God is worthy of reverence and must be declared transcendent from what does not befit His attributes.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه أهل أن يعظم وينزه عما لا يليق بصفاته

TABRISI:55:24-29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r10.claim: Arabic idiom uses “face of the opinion” or “face of the plan” for the opinion or plan itself; al-A'sha's poem uses face for the settled judgment.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r10.anchor: وتقول العرب هذا وجه الرأي وهذا وجه التدبير بمعنى أنه الرأي والتدبير

TABRISI:55:24-29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:55:24-29/r11.claim: Another interpretation makes “face” the means by which one draws near to God, supported by a poem pairing God's face with deeds.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد بالوجه ما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى

TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.claim: Death is a favor because it equalizes creatures, leads to reward, warns that worldly life ends, and gives moral agency: immediate reward would compel action and erase its merit.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.anchor: النعمة فيه التسوية بين الخلق فيه وأيضا فإنه وصلة إلى الثواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.claim: They report that the angels concluded the people of earth had perished when this verse was revealed, then became certain of their own destruction when 28:88 was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: لما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة: هلك أهل الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.speaker: الشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says a reader should not pause after the statement that all on earth perish, but continue into the statement that the Lord's face remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.anchor: قال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} فلا تسكت حتى تقول: {ويبقى وجه ربك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the Face to mean the Lord's manifestation through His signs, just as a human face makes the person apparent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أن المعنى ويبقى ربك الظاهر بأدلته كظهور الإنسان بوجهه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes Face as a term for something eminent, so the phrase means the Lord, the exalted Master.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r5.anchor: الثاني: ويبقى ربك وهو السيد المعظم، والوجه يذكر بمعنى الشيء المعظم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r6.claim: Dhū is an adjective of wajh; if wajh were merely an adjunct of rabbika, the adjective would be dhī rather than nominative dhū.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الوجه هاهنا صلة لقوله (ذو) بالرفع وهو من صفة الوجه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r7.claim: Jalāl denotes God's greatness and majesty and His right to praised attributes for His beneficence and favor; the word derives from jalla, to be great.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r7.anchor: والجلال عظمة الله وكبرياؤه واستحقاقه صفات المدح بإحسانه وإنعامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r8.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says jalāl is used only of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r8.anchor: قال الأصمعي: ولا يقال الجلال إلا لله تبارك وتعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r9.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r9.claim: Abu Ali cites poetry in which jalāl describes someone other than God, while allowing that the poem may be pre-Islamic and that al-Asmaʿi meant only God deserves the term after Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: قد جاء الجلال في غير الله سبحانه وأنشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r10.claim: Ikram can mean God's honoring His prophets through grace, or servants honoring God through worship and praise for His favors.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r10.anchor: وللإكرام هاهنا معنيان. أحدهما: إكرام الله تعالى أنبياءه فهو مكرمهم بلطفه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r11.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r11.claim: Hasan and al-Kalbi take ikram as God's honoring the people of His religion and loyalty and His generosity in forgiving His creatures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r11.anchor: والأول معنى قول الحسن: الذي يكرم أهل دينه وولايته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas takes ikram as meaning that none is more honorable, majestic, or great than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r12.anchor: والثاني معنى قول ابن عباس: الذي لا أكرم منه ولا أجل ولا أعظم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r7.anchor: ويبقى وجه ربك } وهو السيد { ذو الجلال } العظمة { والإكرام } لأنبيائه وأوليائه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r8.claim: He is possessed of majesty and of honoring His prophets and friends.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r8.anchor: ذو الجلال } العظمة { والإكرام } لأنبيائه وأوليائه.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.claim: After enumerating worldly blessings, the passage reminds readers that they and their inhabitants are finite while absolute permanence belongs only to God; lasting happiness calls for a life pleasing to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.anchor: bütün bunların geçici ve üzerinde yaşayanların sonlu olduğu, mutlak anlamda kalıcılığın ise Allah Teâlâ’ya mahsus bulunduğu hatırlatılarak

BURHAN:v2p51/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p51/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p51/r6.claim: The permanence of the Lord’s face does not conflict with the statement that all on earth perish.

ITQAN:v3p13/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p13/r1.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة
ITQAN:v3p13/r1.claim: The majority of Sunnis, including the early authorities and hadith scholars, affirm the attribute verses, consign their intended meaning to God, and deny that their literal realities apply to Him.
ITQAN:v3p13/r1.anchor: وجمهور أهل السنة منهم السلف وأهل الحديث على الإيمان بها وتفويض معناها المراد منها إلى الله تعالى

ITQAN:v3p13/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p13/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
ITQAN:v3p13/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan says the jurists unanimously affirmed the divine attributes without interpretation or likening God to creation.
ITQAN:v3p13/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن الحسن قال إتفق الفقهاء كلهم من المشرق إلى المغرب على الإيمان بالصفات من غير تفسير ولا تشبيه

ITQAN:v3p13/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p13/r7.speaker: سفيان الثوري ومالك وابن المبارك وابن عيينة ووكيع
ITQAN:v3p13/r7.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says these leading imams transmit the reports as received and believe them, without asking how, interpreting, or imagining their modality.
ITQAN:v3p13/r7.anchor: قال الترمذي في الكلام على حديث الرؤية المذهب في هذا عند أهل العلم من الأئمة مثل سفيان الثوري ومالك وابن المبارك

ITQAN:v3p13/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p13/r8.speaker: طائفة من أهل السنة
ITQAN:v3p13/r8.claim: A later Sunni group interprets the attribute verses in a way fitting God’s majesty; this is the position of the later scholars.
ITQAN:v3p13/r8.anchor: وذهبت طائفة من أهل السنة على أننا نؤولها على ما يليق بجلاله تعالى وهذا مذهب الخلف

ITQAN:v3p13/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p13/r9.speaker: إمام الحرمين
ITQAN:v3p13/r9.claim: Al-Juwayni first held figurative interpretation, then recanted and said the doctrine he accepted was to follow the early Muslims, who left the meanings unprobed.
ITQAN:v3p13/r9.anchor: وكان إمام الحرمين يذهب إليه ثم رجع عنه فقال في الرسالة النظامية الذي نرتضيه دينا وندين الله به عقدا إتباع سلف الأمة

ITQAN:v1p222/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says not to pause after 55:26 but to continue reading through 55:27; Suyuti says Ibn Abi Hatim recorded this.
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.anchor: وصح عن الشعبي أنه قال إذا قرأت ﴿ كل من عليها فان ﴾ فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ ﴿ ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام ﴾

ITQAN:v3p236/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.claim: Iftinān joins two modes, praise and consolation: God comforts all creatures capable of life by announcing their end, then praises His own abiding majesty and generosity in ten words.
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.anchor: هو الإتيان في كلام بفنين مختلفين كالجمع بين الفخر والتعزية في قوله تعالى ﴿ كل من عليها فان ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام ﴾

BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.speaker: الملائكة
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.claim: The angels first thought the children of Adam had perished when this verse was revealed; after 'every soul tastes death' was revealed, they realized they too would die, since their subtle bodies and attached spirits perish, though the lofty, immaterial spirits do not.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة : هلكت بنوا آدم

BURSEVI:v9p243/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p243/r7.claim: The 'face' of the Lord means His essence; face, the noblest bodily member and locus of the senses, is borrowed as an expression for the essence.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r7.anchor: أي ذاته ومنه كرم الله وجهه أي ذاته فالوجه العضو المعروف استعير للذات

BURSEVI:v9p243/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r8.speaker: القاضي
BURSEVI:v9p243/r8.claim: Al-Qadi says that examining the aspects of all existing things shows them to be perishing in themselves, except for the face of God turned toward His direction.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r8.anchor: قال القاضي : لو استقريت جهات الموجودات وتفحصت وجوهها

BURSEVI:v9p243/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r9.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p243/r9.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti suggests that 'face' can mean aim or intention, and that the phrase about directions is loosely worded, with the genitive explaining the aim toward which one turns.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r9.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي في حاشية هذا المحل إشارة إلى وجه آخر وهو أن يكون الوجه بمعنى القصد

BURSEVI:v9p243/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r10.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v9p243/r10.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says 'face' may mean direction, since no direction lacks a face toward which one turns; he connects this to the expression 'in God's side.'
BURSEVI:v9p243/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ إشارة إلى أن الوجه يجوز أن يكون كناية عن الجهة بناء على أن كل جهة

BURSEVI:v9p243/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r11.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v9p243/r11.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh adds that earthly beings and their works perish except what they direct toward God and do in pursuit of His good pleasure.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r11.anchor: وأما اكتسبوه من الأعمال هالك إلا ما توجهوا به جهة الله وعملوه ابتغاء لمرضاته

BURSEVI:v9p244/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r1.claim: Dhu al-Jalal wa-al-Ikram describes God as absolutely self-sufficient or majestic in essence and attributes, and as possessing complete generosity.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r1.anchor: ذو الاستغناء المطلق أو العظمة في ذاته وصفاته وذو الفضل التام

BURSEVI:v9p244/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p244/r2.claim: The Prophet urges people to persist in invoking God by the name 'Possessor of Majesty and Generosity.'
BURSEVI:v9p244/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ألظوا بياذا الجلال والإكرام

BURSEVI:v9p244/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p244/r3.claim: The Prophet passed a man praying with this invocation and told him his supplication had been answered, so calling on God by these two names is likely to be accepted.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r3.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام أنه مر برجل وهو يصلي ويقول : يذا الجلال والإكرام

BURSEVI:v9p244/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r4.claim: Mentioning God's majesty and generosity after creation's perishing signals that He will still bestow kindness after their death; resurrection to eternal life and abiding bliss is the greatest blessing.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r4.anchor: وفي وصفه تعالى بذلك بعد ذكر فناء الخلق وبقائه تعالى إيذان بأنه تعالى يفيض عليهم بعد فنائهم أيضا آثار لطفه وكرمه

BURSEVI:v9p244/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r5.claim: The singular 'your Lord' in the first phrase expands the address to everyone fit to be addressed, especially including humans and jinn because of the matter's gravity; the next dual address remains literal.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r5.anchor: اقتضى الأول تعميم الخطاب لكل من يصلح للخطاب لعظم الأمر وفخامته فيندرج فيه الثقلان

BURSEVI:v9p244/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r8.claim: God's abiding face signifies the passing of relative multiplicity among the Names and the abiding of essential, real unity, characterized by both severity and gentleness.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r8.anchor: وبقوله ويبقى وجه الخ إشارة إلى فناء الكثرة النسبية الأسمائية وبقاء الوحدة الحقيقية الذاتية الموصوفة بالصفة الجلالية القهرية والجمالية اللطفية

BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.claim: Some say that deeper discernment reveals the actual perishing of the universe even while it appears to exist, since what depends on another is not truly self-subsisting; real existence belongs to the pre-eternal.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو نظرت بنظر التحقيق في الكون وأهله لرأيت حقيقة فنائه وفناء أهله

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r3.claim: He takes the enduring face of the Lord to mean God’s Essence, as in 28:88; the grammatical agreement that follows supports this reading.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r3.anchor: “vech” كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُۥ’de [el-Kasas 28/88] olduğu gibi Zât-ı Rab mânasına olduğu anlaşılıyor.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r4.claim: The nominative “Dhu” makes majesty and generosity an adjective of “face”; if it modified “Lord,” it would be genitive.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r4.anchor: “Zü’l-celâli ve’l-ikrâm” sıfatı “zû” diye merfu olarak “vech”e sıfat yapılmıştır. Eğer öyle olmasa idi

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r5.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r5.claim: Al-Qadi Baydawi glosses the face as the Essence, while also allowing it to mean the direction toward God or a direction He possesses.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r5.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî “Zât” ile tefsir ettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: “Mevcûdâtın cihetlerini istikrâ

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r6.speaker: Şihâb
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r6.claim: Shihab calls this an alternative exegesis: “face” means the direction toward which one aims, not a metaphor for the Essence.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r6.anchor: Hâşiyesinde Şihâb bunu şöyle îzah etmiştir: “Bu diğer bir tefsirdir.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r7.speaker: Makdisî
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r7.claim: Makdisi says contingent things are inherently liable to nonexistence; only the side God turns toward and grants existence is excepted.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r7.anchor: Üstadımız Makdisî kaddesallahu rûhahu dedi ki: ‘Haddizâtında adem olanda asıl, kendi zatı itibariyle

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r8.claim: Without God’s regard and bestowal of existence, contingent things would have no existence and remain absent.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r8.anchor: Hakk’ın ona nazarı ve hil‘at-i vücûdu ifazası olmasa idi onun için vücud şerefi hâsıl olmazdı

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r9.claim: Some exegetes take “face” to mean righteous deeds done to draw near to God.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r9.anchor: Şu hâlde bazı tefsirlerde olduğu gibi “vech” ile amel-i sâlih murad olunmak da mümkin olur.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r10.claim: A righteous deed is kept for its doer until God rewards it, so its reward remains in place of the deed.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r10.anchor: abd, onu emre imtisâlen işleyince Allah ona mükâfâtını verinceye kadar onu onun için ibkā eder.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r11.speaker: Meşâyıhımızdan bazısı
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r11.claim: Some of the author’s shaykhs identify the imperishable face with God’s sustaining care of created things, an attribute of the divine Essence.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r11.anchor: Meşâyıhımızdan bazısı da şöyle dedi: O adem-i fenâ ile mevsuf olan vech, Allah teâlâ’nın mevcûdâta kayyûmiyetidir.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r12.claim: On the Salaf approach, affirm the reported attributes such as face and hand without asking how they are or interpreting them.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r12.anchor: Selef mezhebince giderek vech, yed gibi sıfatları isbat eder

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r13.speaker: Muhakkikler
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r13.claim: The realized knowers refuse to witness anything besides God because they recognize His sustaining and abiding encompassment of all things.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r13.anchor: bazı ârifler demişlerdir ki muhakkikler Allah teâlâ’nın gayrısına şehadetten ibâ ettiler. Çünkü O, onları şuhûd-ı kayyûmiyyet

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r14.speaker: İbn Atâ
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r14.claim: Ibn Ata says created existence is darkness, illuminated only by God’s manifestation; whoever sees creation without witnessing God in, before, after, or alongside it is veiled from the lights of knowledge.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r14.anchor: İbn Atâ demiştir ki kevn, hep zulmettir. Onu ancak Hak teâlâ’nın onda zuhûru nurlandırmaktadır.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r15.claim: Although “face” can denote created beings’ God-facing relation and their benefit from divine lordship and emanation, the majesty-and-generosity epithet rules these readings out here and identifies God’s Essence.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r15.anchor: Hâsılı, Allah yüzü eşyânın veya insanların Allah’a bakan yüzü, yani kendi zatlarına nazaran değil de Allah teâlâ’nın rubûbiyetinden

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r16.claim: Calling it God’s face rather than simply saying “your Lord remains” emphasizes the permanence of the Essence through the manifestation of attributes and lordship; the sustaining-attribute reading makes this point too.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r16.anchor: Bunun nüktesi Zât’ın yalnız bâtında ve mücerred zat olarak değil, sıfât[^10]

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r17.claim: Majesty signifies absolute greatness and self-sufficiency that overwhelms all; generosity gives existence and complete care even to the nonexistent and perishing.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r17.anchor: azamet ve celâli ile her şeyi kahr u ifnâ edebilecek derecede büyüklük ve istiğnâ-yı mutlak sâhibi, hem de ma‘dum ve fânîlere vücud vererek

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r18.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r18.claim: Raghib says the attribute “Possessor of Majesty and Generosity” is exclusive to God and is among His most particular attributes.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r18.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “İşbu Zü’l-celâli ve’likrâm sıfatı Allah teâlâ’ya mahsus olan ve O’nun gayrısında kullanılmayan sıfatlardandır.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r19.speaker: Enes, Rebî‘a b. Âmir
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r19.claim: A Prophetic report transmitted by Tirmidhi from Anas and Ahmad from Rabi'a ibn Amir urges frequent, steadfast repetition of “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity” in supplication.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r19.anchor: Tirmizî’nin Enes’ten, İmam Ahmed’in Rebî‘a b. Âmir’den merfû‘an rivayet ettikleri şu hadîs-i şerîf de buna şehadet eder

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r20.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r20.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet calls a prayer invoking God’s praise, generosity, majesty, life, and self-subsistence a supplication by the Greatest Name, which ensures a response and grants what is asked.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r20.anchor: Bunun üzerine Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ashâbına buyurdu ki: “Biliyor musunuz ne ile dua etti?”

ITQAN:v3p98/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.claim: The reverse figure names a part for the whole: 'face' means God's essence or the person facing, body-wide states are expressed by faces or hands, and prayer's standing, reciting, bowing, or prostrating can stand for the whole prayer.
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.anchor: عبر بالوجوه عن جميع الأجساد لأن التنعم والنصب حاصل بكلها

ITQAN:v2p332#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p332#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p332#2/r9.claim: Dhu al-jalal means possessing majesty and greatness.

ITQAN:v3p17/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p17/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v3p17/r5.claim: Mujahid treats the hand as an emphatic addition like “the Face of your Lord”; al-Baghawi rejects this as weak, since it would erase Adam’s distinction from Satan.
ITQAN:v3p17/r5.anchor: قال البغوي وهذا تأويل غير قوي لأنها لو كانت صلة لكان لإبليس أن يقول

NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.claim: Ibn Dhakwan differs in reports on imāla for عمران, الإكرام, and إكراههن; the Tajrid records only imāla, through al-Akhfash and several transmitters.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r5.anchor: وأما عمران، وهو في قوله آل عمران، وامرأة عمران، ابنت عمران والإكرام وهو الموضعان في سورة الرحمن، إكراههن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r8.claim: Dhu al-jalāl describes the Lord as possessing majesty and greatness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r8.anchor: {ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال} ، ذو العظمة والكبرياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r9.claim: Al-ikrām means that, despite His majesty, God graciously honors His prophets and friends.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r9.anchor: {والإكرام} ، أي مكرم أنبيائه وأوليائه بلطفه مع جلاله وعظمته.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r1.claim: The repeated question about denied favors follows God's enduring, majestic and generous face: His treatment of creatures reflects greatness and generosity that does not cease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r1.anchor: وتفريع { فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان } إنما هو تفريع على جملة { ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام }
